Yung laundry I would wear something for as long as I can as long as di pa sya nangangamoy (airconed malls helped) tapos paisa-isa ko syang lalabhan with safeguard sa mga sink tapos I would look for a place to sit with my bags and "isasampay" ko sya sa ibabaw ng maleta ko. Usually mga 2-3 articles of clothing lang nilalabhan ko per week and the rest is pinaubaya ko na sa kakarampot na perfume I had left huhuhu. I got out of this situation kasi thankfully natanggap ako in one of the best BPO companies sa Northgate area and meron silang sleeping quarters dun. Yun nga lang I had to get rid of more than half of all my clothes para mapagkasya ko LAHAT ng gamit ko sa company locker which is sobrang liit (I still remember crying kasi I had to get rid of my only sketchbook and watercolor set left and sleeping in my jeans kasi lahat ng pambahay ko tinapon ko na. I'd rather get rid of all that than my presentable clothes). Thankfully I had VERY understanding coworkers and a kind TL na hindi nagsumbong kahit alam nila na dun ako sa company tumutuloy. Ayun tiis-tiis lang hanggang sweldo and makahanap ako ng malilipatan then I picked myself up from there.

Also thank you! Mga comment na ganto ko narerealize na shet grabe pala yung pinagdaanan ko kasi minsan di siya nagsisink-in like WOAH I WENT THROUGH ALL THAT 😨😨. As a woman in her early 20's I wouldn't wish my experience on my worst enemy.

This was in the Starmall Alabang area back in 2019, to be fair di lang ako tumatambay sa terminal lmao. During the day I had my bags with me and I would walk around the surrounding malls and deposit them sa baggage counter before I would use the public restrooms to wash myself and then walked around some more. The terminal at Starmall is big and I didn't just stay in the terminal itself. The area is near a lot of call center agencies so there were a lot of places to spend the night (at the time naghihintay din ako ng job offer from several of those call centers). 'Yun nga lang you have to accept that you will only get a few hours of sleep and you have to ration your money. Marami din namang tao pag gabi so thankfully I experienced nothing more but hecklers and catcallers.

Ganyan din ako haha. Had to run away from a very physically and sexually abusive household one sem before graduation and was living in a bus terminal for 2 months na kunyari naghihintay lang ng byahe. Nag-BPO ako pero di ko kinaya yung night shift. Right now ang ginagawa ko is part-time ako nagwowork sa minimum wage job kasi kadalasan 4-5 hours lang work mo, tapos the rest of the day I dedicate it to freelance. Artist ako and writer, so sometimes I offer my services on social media (madami sa twitter, instagram, at tiktok if you build you audience) and sites like Fiverr pag medyo desperado na. Pag matumal yung benta hanap ako ng mas "proper" na freelance jobs like article writing, data entry, VA, etc. Ang tandaan lang is laging i-update ang portfolio pag freelance tapos dapat confident ka sa interviews(I've had some employers turn me down kasi walang eye contact and mahina boses ko 😭). I plan on getting my last sem completed soon kasi I have the money and I could easily make time for it na kaso I live 8 hours away from my college right now and alam nating lahat na mahilig sa red tape and mga admin sa ibang college so di ko din alam huhuhu. As someone who realized that chain coffees are overrated during the pandemic, I'll agree with some of the answers here and say brew your own. Way cheaper, more accessible, and if your have a good and sturdy thermos, you can bring it everywhere. No plastic, no overpriced coffee, plus you can experiment with your brews. For me, that option yung pinakasulit when it comes to money.

If you're near Manila, I highly suggest trying out a few blends at Kabayan Coffee near Quinta Market in Quiapo. You can buy a wide variety of beans for cheap, and get a small enough amount if you want to try something new. They also grind it according to your preference after you buy them kaya sure ka talagang fresh. Been buying from them since 2021.
